head: 9e13b0920632d8707c0622f67c53b0a8e513c98a
summary:
This attempt closes O-017 and adds nothing new to fix.

**What changed between 3143629 and 9e13b09**
- `.taad/fitness.yaml:810` now holds the bounded pattern I proposed last pass, character for character. Both skipped spans end at their own first closing tag: `<!--(?:(?!-->).)*-->` and `(?:(?!</ScrollViewer\.\1>).)*`.
- The rule's `because` gains one accurate sentence naming S13.
- `eng/rules-harness/plants.json` adds S13, a quiet row that plants `<!-- the texts -->` after the unique anchor `</ScrollViewer.Style>`. The `_note` now says 35 rows, which adds up: 19 + 3 + 8 + 5.
- Nothing under `src/` or `tests/` has changed since f513faf, so the window-case evidence from the first review still describes the shipped code.

**What I checked**
I loaded harness.py's own `Planting` class and ran `taad3.fitness.check` on a scratch copy holding only the SL-065 rule. With F06 and S09–S13 planted in one batch, as a full plants run groups them:

| Tree | Planted at | Rule hits |
|---|---|---|
| Clean | – | none (pass) |
| Batch: F06, S09–S13 | F06 107; S09 108; S10 111; S11 115; S12 119; S13 320 | 108, 111, 115, 119 |
| S13 alone | 300 | none (pass) |
| S12 with S13 | S12 107; S13 308 | 107 |

- Each fire row hits exactly its own first line.
- S13 stays quiet.
- There are no stray hits.
- S13's anchor resolves to the original `</ScrollViewer.Style>`, not the copy S12 plants, because Planting only matches lines it did not plant.
- Restoring the file brings the result back to a clean pass.

Also run:
- The Fitness tool on the real tree: every rule holds.
- `rules-parity`: AGREE, still 47 settled entries.

**Adversarial pass on the pattern**
- Linear time: the tempered tokens and the quoted-attribute alternation are unambiguous.
- `\s` covers CRLF, a lone CR and tabs.
- Nothing I tried produced a false positive.
- Two XML-legal false negatives remain:
  - an end tag written `</ScrollViewer.Style >` with a space before the `>`;
  - an empty self-closing property element before the list.

  Neither is a shape this file or its formatter produces, so I have not filed them.

**Statements elsewhere**
The MainWindow.xaml comment, the S09 note and the rule's `because` all still describe the pattern correctly.

Second round: The rule still fires on text inside an XML comment, which no earlier pass caught. The fix below also closes two false negatives I had noted last pass but not filed.

**What I measured.** I ran the engine's `taad3.fitness.check` on scratch copies of MainWindow.xaml. The rule at `.taad/fitness.yaml:810` fires on:
- a commented-out one-line example, `<!-- never write <ScrollViewer><ListBox /></ScrollViewer> here -->`, at line 107;
- the same example spread over several lines inside a comment, at 108;
- a commented example placed next to a real violation, which gives two hits, 107 and 108, instead of one.

**Why it happens.** For .xaml the engine does not blank `<!-- -->` comments, so this settled entry, which has no `including_comments` flag, also matches comment text. That contradicts the file's own header at `fitness.yaml:57-60`: "a settled entry without the flag is matched against code only".

**The two false negatives** the same edit closes:
- an end tag written with a space, `</ScrollViewer.Style >`, which XML allows;
- a self-closing property element such as `<ScrollViewer.Resources />` before the list.

**The fix.** One edit to the pattern: skip a `<ScrollViewer` that sits inside a comment, and accept those two property-element forms. I checked it with harness.py's own `Planting` class and the engine:
- The clean tree passes.
- F06 plus S09–S13 in one batch hit exactly 108, 111, 115 and 119 with no stray.
- S13 stays quiet, and so do the DriveScroller comment, the self-closing sibling and both in-comment examples.
- It still fires on '>' in an attribute, the comment/Resources/comment/DataGrid shape, a tab-indented S11, an empty comment between the tags, and both false-negative shapes.
- The commented example beside a real violation gives only the real hit.

**Otherwise unchanged since the last pass.**
- Nothing under `src/` or `tests/` has changed since f513faf.
- The Fitness tool reports every rule holds on the real tree.
- rules-parity: AGREE.

findings.claim: The SL-065 rule fires on a ScrollViewer and list written inside an XML comment: a commented-out block, or a documentation example of what not to do. For .xaml the engine does not blank `<!-- -->` comments, so this settled entry without `including_comments` matches comment text. A future slice that comments out such a block, or writes the anti-pattern as an example next to the contract comment, gets a false failing gate pointing at the comment. Beside a real violation it reports two hits instead of one, which the harness would count as a stray. Two XML-legal false negatives remain in the same pattern: an end tag with whitespace (`</ScrollViewer.Style >`) and a self-closing property element (`<ScrollViewer.Resources />`) before the list.

S09-S12 still fire at their first planted line under the bounded pattern. Comment-first and ScrollViewer.Style-first lists are caught, and the self-closing sibling stays quiet.
No src/tests change since f513faf (git diff --stat empty). The S-002 and S-008 results stand.
No src change. The S-007 result and the stripRows formula probe stand.

cases.evidence: Deferred as material:false, and the reason now holds. The rule fires on the house-style shapes (S11, S12) and stays quiet on a legitimate commented ScrollViewer (S13). Verified with the harness's Planting and the engine.

drift: No undeclared departure. Declared: S13's text is indented to the house style, and the rule's `because` gains one sentence. Unchanged and on the open list: eng/rules-harness/harness.py still cannot run end to end at this HEAD, so S09-S13 are proven only through its components and not by an unattended run.

No undeclared departure; the build used the reviewer's pattern verbatim. The in-comment false positive is filed as M1. This rule's pattern has now been corrected three times. harness.py still cannot run end to end at this HEAD, so an unattended run of these plant rows is what would stop a fourth regression.
